tag: Episode 2 · A Cat in a Hat? Yeongnyangi
title: A Cat in a Hat? Yeongnyangi

beats.t: The leaf boat touched the landing of the Island of Companions. Tap. Quieter than she'd expected.
The pursuing black hands stopped short of the island. They writhed briefly beyond the mist, then sank beneath the river.
Yeoni caught her breath, still gripping the leaf's edge. Her short forelegs were rigid with effort.
I'm alive...
A little snort slipped out after the words. Oink. Yeoni immediately clamped a hoof over their mouth.
No. That was just breathing. Not a pig noise.
Yeongnyangi. Someone waved from a mirror. With a human hand.
I saw.
…It was me. In my hoodie.
Then be careful. This is the Island of Companions.
What's that supposed to mean? Briefly.
Those standing on the same side as you. Friends, competitors, pride.
Why fight if we're on the same side?
Because you want the same place.
…That really was brief. Four stars.
Yeongnyangi hopped lightly onto the landing. Golden pawprints bloomed on the black glass floor, then vanished.
Wow. Add sound effects and this would be a game.
You still think this is a game?
I haven't given up hope. One loading screen, and I'll accept it.
Still working hard to find another explanation.
I'll take that as a compliment. But what are you? A cat in a hat, or a cat doing cosplay?
...Not an ordinary cat.
Except you keep looking like a cat.
Say that once more, and I'll leave those pawprints on your forehead.
Yes, yes, Lord Cat. Lord Cat of the Magnificent Hat.
Yeoni tried to climb carefully off the leaf. She set her forelegs down, then began moving her hind legs.
Uh, whoa?
Their short legs refused to cooperate. Yeoni landed nose-first on the dock. Thud.
Her nose stung. Her pride stung more.
Your landings need practice.
Stop analyzing me.
Isn't this the kind of thing that comes with a tutorial? No controls, no save function, not even a refund button.
A snort escaped at the end of her protest. Oink. It cut the weight of her objection neatly in half.
The island was silent. No grass, houses, or people. It seemed built entirely of mirror fragments.
The floor shone like black glass. Mirrors large and small floated in the air, from palm-sized to door-sized, each tilted a different way.
Mirrors reflecting the sky. The river. The leaf boat. And Yeoni.
She peered into a nearby mirror. A flower pig looked back: pink body, short forelegs, a little flower on its head. One petal was still faded white.
Far too cute. She hated it.
I still can't get used to this.
When did my cheeks get so chubby? Did someone secretly pump air into them?
When Yeoni lifted a foreleg, the flower pig did the same, reversed left to right. She tilted her head; it copied her exactly.
Hey. Stop copying me.
The flower pig silently mouthed the words too. Infuriating.
She turned this way and that, and her tail swayed with her. Its cuteness only irritated her more.
Hey. Mess up just once. Lag a little, and I'll admit you're the fake.
Oh, seriously.
What's wrong?
My whole aesthetic was supposed to be cool and badass. Now someone's switched my genre to soothing animal cuteness.
…I can't tell whether you're pleased or not.
You wouldn't understand. Having your entire appearance change genres overnight.
I have been a finished masterpiece since birth.
Oh, yes. Of course you have.
Traveling-cat review: two stars for personality. Half a star extra for the pretty hat.
She brushed it off and walked farther inland. The mirror shards grew denser as she went. Then she stopped.
One mirror wasn't reflecting a flower pig. It was the mirror she'd been looking for.
There was a person inside.
Wet hair. A loose hoodie. Sweatpants baggy at the knees. A charger cable tossed on the bed. A phone in one hand.
A twenty-three-year-old student looking wearily down at a screen. The original Yeoni. So familiar she seemed strange.
Yeoni slowly approached. Each hoofstep made a small tap against the floor.
The Yeoni in the mirror sat on her bed, just as she'd been in reality. Hair loosely tied, fatigue still on her face. Still the face Yeoni knew as her own.
Human hands. Human legs. Human eyes. Everything she had lost was there, one thin pane away.
She looked down at her forelegs, then back at the mirror. Something tightened in her chest.
I... looked like that, didn't I?
Her voice came out smaller than expected. Her throat kept closing.
Forgotten sensations returned all at once. Swiping across a screen with a finger. The hair tie resting around their wrist before they tied their hair.
The irritation of throwing off wet socks. The blank despair before a ruined assignment file. All those little things had become impossibly far away.
Yeoni raised a hoof to the cold mirror. Her reflection raised a hand. A human palm and a short foreleg met across one sheet of glass.
Tears rose in her throat. She truly wanted to go home.
Until a moment ago, wanting to go home had been half a joke. Now it was real.
I want to go home. To my room. My bed. My fingers.
...Yeongnyangi.
I'm listening. Go on.
Is that... really me?
Yeongnyangi looked into the mirror. His expression grew more serious too.
Your original appearance.
Then if I go in there, can I go back?
No.
The answer was quick and firm. Unable to look away, Yeoni asked.
...Why?
This island's mirrors aren't exits.
Then what?
They only reflect the place you left behind.
Yeoni didn't answer. She slowly took her hoof from the glass.
Then the Yeoni in the mirror moved. Yeoni held her breath.
Until now, the mirror had copied her. Now it was the other way around.
The human Yeoni wore a different expression: calmer, straighter, confident in a way Yeoni wasn't.
You're late.
Yeoni froze.
...What?
You're always late.
A small remark, sharp as a nail. Yeoni stepped back before she knew it.
Late for alarms, late replying, late apologizing, late for every chance.
A thin crack appeared across the mirror.
Late again today.
Yeoni bit their lip.
What are you?
Me? Yeoni.
That was the answer Yeoni hated most. They tapped their chest with a hoof.
I'm Yeoni.
Really? In that body?
Words failed her. She was angry, but couldn't answer back.
The mirror Yeoni looked so natural. Her room, her voice, her face, her expression.
If someone had to choose the real Yeoni, would they choose the pink flower pig, or that person?
Be careful.
What is that thing?
A reflection made by the island. A rival wearing your face.
So, a doppelgänger.
In simple terms, yes.
My life really is squeezing in every possible trope.
You are not here as a spectator.
There's no place for you here.
The words echoed across the island. Nearby mirrors lit one after another, each showing a different scene.
The back row of a lecture hall. A seat someone else had already taken. Yeoni's message posted too late in the group-project chat. An unread reply.
A text canceling an interview. A contest entry that had failed to submit. And a single rice triangle lying on a convenience-store floor.
Hey, leave the rice triangle out of this. That's too pathetic.
She meant it as a joke, but her voice wavered. Each incident alone was something she could laugh off.
Together, they felt like being pushed aside. A little later, a little farther back, missing things until eventually she'd be no one at all.
Then one enormous mirror slowly rose. Deep blue light circled its watery surface.
A human Yeoni stood within it too. Beneath her feet was the black river, not her bedroom floor.
A tiny shoot grew at that Yeoni's feet. Deep currents rippled beneath it.
[ 乙亥 ]
Yeoni couldn't take her eyes off the two characters appearing at the mirror's edge.
Eulhae. The characters she'd seen on her phone. Back then they had been unfamiliar; now they felt like a name she'd known forever. The flower on her head glowed faintly.
Found it.
Found what?
Your Day Pillar. The pillar of the day you were born.
The Eulhae Day Pillar.
Eulhae...
Speaking the words made her flower glow brighter. The human Yeoni saw it too. For the first time, her expression stiffened.
No.
The mirror Yeoni reached out. [乙亥] began sliding from the mirror's edge toward her.
Yeoni, stop it!
How!
Hold on to your name!
What does that mean? Say it so I can understand!
It means don't let her take your place!
You hate being you right now.
Yeoni hesitated.
You hate that body, being here, and the bad luck waiting in your real life.
The reflection stepped forward. The mirror rippled like water.
Look. You've already thrown away a petal.
Yeoni covered the faded petal with a hoof. Hiding it didn't bring its color back.
So let me do it. I'm the real Yeoni.
Yeoni's heart plunged.
I'll go back in your place.
Yeoni couldn't breathe. The reflection was so convincing: a familiar face, normal hands, a normal voice.
That girl had everything Yeoni had lost.
Even if you went home looking like that, nobody would believe you're you.
The words lodged in Yeoni's throat. They looked down at their hooves. Pink. Short and round. Cute, but nothing like themself.
Just for a moment. What if that girl went back instead? What if she was better at being Yeoni?
The thought itself chilled her.
Don't listen to her.
But...
The mirror slips into the gap where you hate yourself.
Yeongnyangi stepped in front of Yeoni.
Your opponent isn't a stranger. It's you, after your own place.
You talk too much.
The mirror Yeoni snapped her fingers. The shards rose at once and rained down on Yeoni and Yeongnyangi.
Get back!
The golden tassel on Yeongnyangi's hat blazed. He leapt and twisted in midair, golden claws knocking away shards. Clink. Clink. Clink.
Fragments scattered. The moment he landed, he crouched again.
Keep your eyes on those characters!
Yeoni glared at the great mirror. Eulhae. The characters wavered between the human Yeoni and the flower pig, unable to choose their owner.
You said they're mine.
Yes. The characters you must recover.
Then why are they trying to go over there?
Answer that yourself. What have you been doing all this time?
Yeoni held her breath. She'd called it a dream. Insisted it was a game. Treated it as another-world fiction.
She'd kept pushing away the self that had become a flower pig. She didn't want to accept it. She was scared.
And the mirror Yeoni had been taking over that gap, little by little.
…I pushed myself out, and let her in.
The reflection reached out again. [乙亥] slid farther toward her. The flower on Yeoni's head trembled precariously.
Yeoni.
Yeoni closed her eyes, then opened them.
She was still afraid. Still wanted home. Still hated this body. Even so.
Hey.
The mirror Yeoni watched her. Yeoni tapped her chest with a forehoof.
I don't like how I look right now either. Not one bit.
No fingers, short legs, and I oink when I'm startled.
A tiny oink actually slipped out.
...See? That annoys me too.
Exactly, so I can—
But.
Yeoni cut her off. Her flower glowed again, brighter than before except for the single faded petal.
But I'm still Yeoni.
The reflected Yeoni's expression hardened.
Even looking like this.
She stepped forward. A small step on short legs. Forward all the same.
Even if I was late.
Another step.
Even if things went wrong.
Another step.
Even if my luck has completely fallen apart.
At last, Yeoni stood before the great mirror.
I decide where I belong.
[乙亥] shuddered. The human Yeoni gritted her teeth.
Not yet. You don't even know what you are.
The mirror cracked open. Deep-blue water poured through, cold and fathomless. From within it, a tiny green shoot unfurled.
乙 — Eul.
Dark blue currents swirled beneath the shoot.
亥 — Hae.
Yin Wood, Yin Water. A small shoot and deep water. The characters in the mirror finally revealed their full shapes.
[ 乙亥 ]
Then the human Yeoni stepped out of the mirror.
The girl who emerged smiled with Yeoni's own face. The two characters [乙亥] settled onto her palm.
Fine. Prove it, then.
Every mirror around them lit up at once.
That you're the real Yeoni. Prove it, and I'll give them back.
Yeoni stared at her own face. The characters lay on that girl's palm. Eulhae. The first pillar she had to recover.
Do not retreat.
Yeoni drew a deep breath. Her faded petal trembled in the breeze.
Right. But first, one thing.
The mirror Yeoni tilted her head. Yeoni narrowed her eyes.
Don't use my face to smirk like that.
The reflection stopped smiling.
